definitions.gloss: Bizen ware; unglazed stoneware from Okayama
definitions.explanation: Stoneware made around Imbe in Bizen, Okayama Prefecture, one of Japan's oldest pottery traditions. It is fired without glaze for many days in wood-burning kilns, and its reddish-brown surface takes its patterns from ash and flame. Valued for tea-ceremony vessels and flower vases.

examples.english: Bizen ware uses no glaze; its colours and patterns come from the clay and the flame alone.

notes:
{備前|びぜん} (the old province, now part of Okayama Prefecture) + ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (ware). Like other ware names (⟦{有田焼|ありたやき}→有田焼：28604_aritayaki⟧, ⟦{信楽焼|しがらきやき}→信楽焼：33327_shigarakiyaki⟧), it is formed with ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Bizen ware is counted among the Six Old Kilns ({日本六古窯|にほんろっこよう}) of Japan. Its plain, earthy look suits the taste called ⟦{侘|わ}び{寂|さ}び→侘び寂び：11691_wabisabi⟧, and fans say beer poured into a Bizen cup has a finer head.
